elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: The added carve-out states that the consent requirement does not apply to Licensee's assignment to an Affiliate.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement to a successor in a merger without consent.
elements.evidence: The added carve-out expressly permits assignment to a successor in a merger without consent.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement to a successor in an acquisition without consent.
elements.evidence: The added carve-out expressly permits assignment to a successor in an acquisition without consent.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: The added carve-out expressly permits assignment to a successor in a sale of substantially all of Licensee's assets without consent.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign the Agreement without Customer's prior consent.
elements.evidence: The clause states that Licensor may not assign the Agreement without Licensee's prior written consent.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to Vendor's assignment.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that Licensee's consent to Licensor's assignment will not be unreasonably withheld, subject to the separate competitor prohibition required by the preferred position.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign the Agreement to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: The clause states that Licensor may not in any event assign the Agreement to a competitor of Licensee.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate the Agreement or Customer's licenses because of Customer's change of control.
elements.evidence: Article XX(a) now states that the Agreement and Licensee's rights and licenses continue in full force and effect even if Licensor has not consented to the Change of Control; no change-of-control termination right remains operative.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement to a successor without consent, subject only to written notice.
elements.evidence: Licensee may assign without consent to successors in the expressly listed standard succession events: merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets. The separate written-notice duty is assessed below.

elements.element: Customer must give Vendor written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: No written-notice obligation applies to Licensee's permitted successor assignments.

elements.element: Vendor may assign the Agreement to a successor without consent, subject only to written notice.
elements.evidence: Licensor remains prohibited from assigning to any successor without Licensee's prior written consent; no successor carve-out is provided for Licensor.

elements.element: Vendor must give Customer written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: No written-notice mechanism is provided for Licensor successor assignments.

elements.element: Customer's assignments other than permitted successor assignments require Vendor's consent.
elements.evidence: The general rule prohibits Licensee from assigning the Agreement or transferring its license rights without Licensor's prior written consent, except for the added Affiliate and successor carve-outs.

elements.element: Vendor may not unreasonably withhold consent to Customer's other assignments.
elements.evidence: The assignment provision does not require Licensor to act reasonably when considering Licensee's non-carve-out assignments. The reasonableness standard in Article XX applies only to Change of Control consent.

elements.element: Vendor's assignments other than permitted successor assignments require Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Licensor may not assign the Agreement without Licensee's prior written consent.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to Vendor's other assignments.
elements.evidence: Although a general non-unreasonable-withholding standard is stated, Licensor is categorically barred from assigning to any Licensee competitor. Thus the standard does not govern all other assignments as the fallback requires.

result.reason: The redline reaches the preferred position: Licensee receives the required Affiliate and M&A-successor carve-outs, Licensor is subject to reasonable-consent and competitor restrictions, and Change of Control no longer terminates the Agreement or licenses. It does not reach the fallback because Licensor lacks a notice-only successor assignment right, neither party has the required successor-assignment notice duty, and the reasonableness standards are incomplete for other assignments. The changes are targeted, but drafting quality is reduced by retaining obsolete Change of Control consent and deemed-withholding language after making consent irrelevant to continued effectiveness.
